question.worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $Y∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(Y\ge y)=P(Z\ge \frac{y-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =7$ and $\sigma =2.$

First, we transform $Y$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\ge 4.62) & =P(Z\ge \frac{4.62-7}{2}) \\  & =P(Z\ge -1.19)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14263116/assets/f96faea70d10478e9ac5fca7f34e76a0b592ddb87dd5749a93807687907f92bc.png)

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge -1.19) & =1-P(Z<-1.19) \\  & =1-P(Z\le -1.19) \\  & =1-Φ(-1.19)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we know that

$$
Φ(-1.19)=0.1170.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge -1.19) & =1-Φ(-1.19) \\  & =1-0.1170 \\  & =0.8830.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that

$$
P(Y\ge 4.62)=0.8830.
$$
